analysis.title: Intelligence weekly #134: South Korea: Balancing AI tailwinds and supply risks (Transformational Innovation Opportunities (TRIO): Artificial Intelligence)
key_insights: UBS CIO stays Neutral on South Korean equities and right-sizes memory to a mid-single-digit exposure within its AI strategy, after the recent correction and higher volatility.
Tech is more than 70% of the MSCI Korea Index. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix together are nearly 63% of the index weight.
UBS sees the recent volatility as uncertainty over timing, positioning and future supply additions, not a deterioration in AI demand.
MSCI Korea trades at about 1.2x price to book, roughly half its June peak and modestly above its 10-year average of about 1.0x.
Tech is expected to contribute more than 200 percentage points of South Korea's expected 2026 EPS growth, making it the dominant driver of market performance.
UBS expects DRAM bit demand growth to accelerate to about 40% y/y in 2027 from about 20% in 2026. NAND demand is expected to stay robust at about 25% y/y.
Near-term industry supply growth should stay constrained because most incremental DRAM wafer capacity is going to HBM and meaningful new NAND capacity outside China is limited.
Agentic AI workloads are lifting demand across the memory stack, including DDR5 for conventional servers and NAND for storage, not only HBM.

MLCC inventory volumes have stabilized after a long drawdown, while inventory values and unit price indices are at record highs. Pricing is the main driver of value growth, which points to supply that is tight relative to demand.

Hyperscalers are securing long-term agreements. Samsung Electro-Mechanics (SEMCO) has disclosed more than KRW 4.3tr of LTAs covering MLCCs, substrates and silicon capacitors, giving demand visibility into 2027 and beyond.

SEMCO plans to raise MLCC capacity from about 124bn units a month in 2026 to 151bn in 2027 and 170bn in 2028, with projected utilization still around 96-97%. Murata is considering accelerating investment, and the two leading memory makers announced aggressive expansion plans.

UBS will watch Samsung Electronics' capacity expansion and HBM yields closely. Faster memory output, better HBM yields or more downstream component production could change supply-demand expectations, and shares may get more volatile as investors focus on when profitability peaks.

Kospi forward P/E is near historical lows and well below global peers, but it largely reflects peak memory and AI component earnings. Consensus revisions have turned negative as memory-led upgrades moderate, and UBS says revisions have historically driven the market more than absolute valuation.

Single-stock leveraged ETF activity is now about 3% of market turnover, down from a peak of about 34% in July. Residual leveraged flows still amplify moves in memory, AI and semiconductor names and keep some global investors cautious.

UBS estimates Kospi earnings fall about 1.1% for every 1% the KRW appreciates. Memory and MLCC suppliers are especially exposed through USD revenue. UBS expects the KRW to weaken modestly near term and then stabilize.

UBS expects memory and MLCC pricing to rise further, but new capacity from early next year, especially in memory, is the main swing factor for volatility. The report holds a measured view on Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and SEMCO and says investors should stay selective.

market_movers.rationale: UBS CIO keeps a Neutral preference on South Korean equities, balancing AI infrastructure exposure against capacity additions, leveraged ETF activity and currency volatility.
SK Hynix is on the UBS CIO AI equity preference list as Most Preferred (added Oct 30 2025). The report takes a measured view of leading memory makers after the pullback.
Samsung Electronics returned to Most Preferred on the Asia's new mobility list on Oct 22 2026. The report is measured on Samsung and watches its capacity expansion and HBM yields.

sector_views.rationale: AI demand supports earnings through 2027, but new capacity from early next year raises price volatility. UBS right-sizes memory to a mid-single-digit exposure within its AI strategy.

earnings_insights: Tech is expected to contribute more than 200 percentage points of South Korea's expected 2026 EPS growth (UBS estimate).
Kospi one-year forward EPS revisions have turned negative as memory-led upgrades moderate (consensus).
UBS estimates Kospi earnings fall about 1.1% for every 1% the KRW appreciates.
SEMCO has disclosed more than KRW 4.3tr of long-term agreements with large global customers.

macro_indicators.reading: about 40% y/y in 2027 vs about 20% in 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: Demand growth accelerates, supporting memory pricing while supply is constrained near term.
Robust storage demand from agentic AI workloads.
Valuation has reset to roughly half the June peak but is still modestly above the long-run average.
A faster KRW rise would hit export-heavy earnings and multiples.

risk_factors: New memory and MLCC capacity from early next year, including Samsung Electronics' expansion and HBM yield improvements.
Negative consensus earnings revisions as memory-led upgrades moderate.
KRW appreciation, which hurts export-heavy earnings.
Residual leveraged ETF flows amplifying volatility in concentrated large-cap memory and AI names.
Heavy concentration in a few cyclical tech industries (memory, MLCC, AI semiconductors).
vol_and_positioning: Single-stock leveraged ETF turnover is about 3% of total market turnover, down from a peak of about 34% in July.
Residual leveraged ETF flows can amplify selling in memory, AI and semiconductor stocks on disappointments through mechanical rebalancing and momentum trading.
UBS expects volatility to rise as the next supply expansion phase approaches, with investors focused on when profitability peaks.

tension_points.bull_case: AI demand broadens across DDR5, HBM and NAND. DRAM bit demand growth is expected to reach about 40% y/y in 2027, supply is constrained near term, and hyperscaler long-term agreements support pricing visibility.
tension_points.bear_case: Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, SEMCO and Murata are expanding capacity, with more memory supply expected from early next year. Consensus revisions have turned negative, and a low P/E mostly reflects peak earnings.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Faster memory output, improved HBM yields or increased downstream component production that shifts expectations for supply-demand balances.

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong AI demand and rising ASP volatility can coexist because profitability is pushing producers to accelerate capacity.
theme_stances.evidence: strong AI demand and rising average selling price (ASP) volatility can coexist

theme_stances.key_argument: AI infrastructure spending should support memory, MLCC and substrate demand through 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: AI infrastructure buildout remains in its early innings rather than approaching a peak
